Alaska completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results (revenue of $869M and a net loss of $113M) are only included for the ~3.5-month stub period from acquisition to year-end [DOC-2]. This means Alaska's FY2024 revenue, costs, and operating income reflect a partial-year consolidation of a new, loss-making entity, whereas Delta, United, Southwest, and American reflect a full year of operations on a consistent entity basis. All five companies do share the same calendar fiscal year (Jan–Dec 2024), so there is no fiscal-year mismatch [DOC-1].

With that caveat noted, here is the operating-efficiency comparison using the disclosed FY2024 figures [DOC-1]:

**Operating margin (Operating income ÷ Total operating revenue):**
- Delta: $5,995M / $61,643M ≈ 9.7%
- United: $5,096M / $57,063M ≈ 8.9%
- American: $2,614M / $54,211M ≈ 4.8%
- Alaska: $570M / $11,735M ≈ 4.9% (partial Hawaiian consolidation distorts this)
- Southwest: $321M / $27,483M ≈ 1.2%

**Fuel + labor costs as % of revenue (a common proxy for controllable cost efficiency):**
- Delta: ($10,566M + $16,161M) / $61,643M ≈ 43.4%
- United: ($11,756M + $16,678M) / $57,063M ≈ 49.8%
- American: ($11,418M + $16,021M) / $54,211M ≈ 50.6%
- Alaska: ($2,506M + $3,588M) / $11,735M ≈ 51.9%
- Southwest: ($5,812M + $12,240M) / $27,483M ≈ 65.7%

All figures per [DOC-1].

On both metrics, Delta Air Lines shows the strongest results — the highest operating margin (~9.7%) and the lowest combined fuel-and-labor cost burden relative to revenue (~43.4%) — indicating it converted revenue into operating profit more efficiently than United, Southwest, American, or Alaska in FY2024. Southwest, by contrast, had by far the weakest cost efficiency, with fuel and labor alone consuming nearly two-thirds of revenue and an operating margin of just 1.2%.

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines had the most efficient cost structure in FY2024, with the highest operating margin (~9.7%) and lowest combined fuel-and-labor costs as a share of revenue (~43.4%) among the five carriers; note that Alaska's figures are not fully comparable due to its partial-year consolidation of the Hawaiian Holdings acquisition.
